已关闭 issue：#10359（审计日志哈希链投毒——先前存在，现已关闭）、#11009（别名重命名未级联权限配置）、#12064（Discord 对等机器人审批绕过）、#12087（工具开关双重保存）、#11952（- 前缀的相对数据目录）、#12312（OIDC 发现端点策略缺口）、#11919（Thinking 框）。

4. 社区热点

  1. Issue #12320 — CI 安全门禁失败（S1，3 条评论）。杠杆率最高的线程：每个发布和合并都依赖解决该 RUSTSEC 公告。需要要么升级依赖，要么提供有范围、有文档的公告例外。
  2. PR #12317 — feat(zerocode): pairing-free OIDC login and saved remote credentials（XL）。吸引了 10+ 后续 issue（#12330–#12340）——证明了对无摩擦远程 onboarding 的高兴趣，但也反映了审查负担：PR head 存在已知粗糙边缘（ledger actor 双前缀、smoke-test 顺序、cert-without-CA 语义、凭证修剪）。
  3. PR #11847 — 原生 Rust XMPP，可选 OMEMO（XL，高风险）及配套 #12015（ChaCha20Poly1305 统一）和 #12319（重复 crate 允许列表）。社区推动渠道广度；这是最大的开放功能列车之一。
  4. PR #12244 — 通过核心 RPC 的范围化仪表盘聊天（XL，do-not-merge，已阻塞）。长期运行的核心架构 PR。

底层需求：(a) 畅通的发布流水线，(b) 更低摩擦的远程登录，(c) 更广泛/更现代的渠道支持，(d) 整合重复的加密/依赖面。

5. Bug 与稳定性

按严重程度排序（除非注明，均为 2026-11-09 提交/更新）：

  • S1 / 工作流阻塞： #12320 — RUSTSEC-2026-0459 在每次构建中导致 Security 任务失败；合并队列和发布陷入死锁。尚无修复 PR。
  • S0 安全（针对开放 PR head 的审查发现；修复 = 合并前修订 PR）：
    • #12311 — macOS Seatbelt 配置文件授予沙箱命令读取所有 home dotfiles（包括 ~/.zeroclaw）的权限（PR #12150）。
    • #12310 — MCP 配置控制桥接授予模型无限制的配置写入权限，且无审批（PR #12275）。
    • #12309 — sessions_prompt 目标范围未强制执行；PR head 无法编译（PR #12258）。
    • #12308 — 会话删除/TTL 后转录和载荷仍可读；无擦除路径。
    • #12307 — 网关会话丢失 gw_ 命名空间 → 对等调用者可跨会话附加。
    • #12306 — Matrix Goal 父轮次绕过 effort_routing 允许列表（cloud_escalation = never）。
    • #12305 — 守护进程级成本限制覆盖可由非 Telegram 渠道上的任何允许列表对等方批准。
    • #12304 — colony 渠道回复将操作员消息泄露给外部成员（PR #11560）。
  • S2： #12330 — 当 zerocode-config.toml 不可读/不可解析时，zerocode 静默回退到本地守护进程（存在错误端点连接风险）；#12325 — 文档规范 URL 指向发布目录，因此每次发布都会重排 SEO URL。
  • S3： #12347 — zerocode 配置写入者可能丢失并发更新（读-改-写，无锁）；#12326 和 #12324 — 已修剪版本和可索引的 rustdoc/404 页面出现文档 404。

6. 功能请求与路线图信号

  • 无需配对仪式的远程访问 — #12317 的 OIDC 自助设备证书引导，按 #12337 由操作员 opt-in 门控。一旦 #12320 清除，是 v0.9.0 的有力候选。
  • 渠道广度与安全 — XMPP/OMEMO（#11847）、未授权入站消息的所有者通知（PR #12346）、Matrix 路由加固（#12306）。
  • 迁移/互操作 — OpenClaw 导入（#12348，已关闭）。
  • Web UX — 配对设备的语音设置（PR #12269）、折叠 Thinking 开关（#11919，已完成）、窄布局修复（#11933，已完成）。
  • 凭证卫生 — 修剪被取代的 OIDC 凭证代次（#12339）并定义 cert-without-CA 语义（#12338）。

预测：下一个版本将以安全加固（沙箱、会话隔离、审批路径）、zerocode OIDC onboarding 和渠道工作为主——完全取决于 #12320。

7. 用户反馈摘要

  • 挫败感： 发布/CI 阻塞（#12320）是最响亮的信号——什么都无法落地；贡献者产出了经过验证的修复却无处合并。
  • 安全敏感用户（自托管/守护进程操作员）提出了具体的隔离关切：沙箱文件访问、跨会话附加、群聊审批滥用和消息泄露。这些读起来是真实的部署痛点，而非理论问题。
  • 移动/Web 用户： 对响应式和 UX 修复（#11933、#11920）表示满意，表明仪表盘在手机上有活跃使用。
  • Onboarding 摩擦： zerocode 用户希望无配对登录，并愿意接受 opt-in 默认值（#12337）；后续 issue 的数量表明该功能被需要，但当前 head 尚未达到生产就绪。
  • 静默失败焦虑： #12330（配置解析失败 → 本地守护进程回退）和 #12347（丢失配置写入）是那种侵蚀 TUI 客户端信任的微妙降级。

8. 待办关注

  • PR #11868（自 2026-10-19 开放，needs-maintainer-review）— 调度前的重复调用抑制；阻塞相关 #11911，并有配套文档 PR #12265 等待处理。
  • PR #11317（自 2026-10-01 开放，XS 文档）— 有界插件 webhook RPC 放置例外；一个月前的一行文档 PR 仍未审查。
  • PR #11847（自 2026-10-19 开放，XL，needs-maintainer-review）— XMPP 渠道列车；需要审查带宽以避免相对 master 的位腐。
  • PR #12244（已阻塞，do-not-merge）— 通过核心 RPC 的仪表盘聊天；高风险且长期存在，面临冲突搅动风险。
  • Issue #12320 — 不算旧，但最紧迫：它是阻塞整个合并队列和下一发布的基石。

所有链接引用 github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw。数据快照：2026-11-09/10 活动窗口。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-10

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-09 23:19 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-10

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity maintenance phase with no new releases in the last 24 hours, but substantial triage and engineering throughput: 500 issues and 500 PRs were touched, with 208 issues closed and 131 PRs merged/closed. The open backlog skews toward stability work — crash-loop/restart reliability, SQLite/session-state integrity, and Windows/Kubernetes deployment failures dominate the top-commented issues. PR activity is concentrated in small, surgical fixes (CLI error surfacing, WebChat rendering, Android/Telegram channel behavior) rather than large features. Overall health is moderate-to-good: strong maintainer responsiveness and many "ready for maintainer look" PRs, but a persistent cluster of P0/P1 reliability defects (Windows startup, update-after-crash paths, session wedging) suggests the update/restart subsystem is the project's current weak point.

2. Releases

None. No new releases or pre-releases were published in the last 24 hours.

3. Project Progress

131 PRs were merged/closed. Notable closed items signaling forward movement:

  • Issue #172628 [CLOSED, P1] — Fresh Gateway start leaving main-agent admission superseded until restart (fix-shape clear, queueable). Link
  • Issue #167506 [CLOSED, P0] — Deleted temporary handoff DB blocking package recovery and future updates. Link
  • Issue #192959 [CLOSED, P1] — Kubernetes fsGroup remount causing credential-directory rejection. Link
  • Issue #175926 / #158966 / #168794 [CLOSED] — SQLite snapshot reclamation, CDP credential leak, and Codex relay 502 issues respectively.
  • PR #196294 [CLOSED] — Knowledge memory save latency on large vaults (~11s → ~2s). Link

Progress is incremental: many closures appear to be stale-bot or resolution triage rather than shipped fixes (several closed items carry stale labels and no linked fix PR), so "closed" should not be read uniformly as "fixed."

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #170956 Windows slow startup / unclean plugin shutdown / schtasks permission error 30 P0, UX release-blocker
2 #166634 SQLite session reclamation checkpoint failure → agent unavailable after crash 27 Session-state
3 #193962 Header-probe timeout fix unreachable via openclaw update from 2026.10.10 21 P0, diamond lobster
4 #166133 MCP integer args coerced to string 16 P2, needs product decision
5 #164394 WebChat transcript jitter (now CLOSED) 15 UX friction
6 #144336 Deferred config-reload restart fails shutdown step 14 P1, crash-loop

Underlying needs: The top threads cluster around a single theme — trustworthy restarts and updates. Users cannot reliably recover from crashes or apply fixes, which both blocks adoption and turns transient bugs into permanent outages. The second theme is session durability: reclamation/lock/checkpoint failures strand agents until manual intervention. The MCP coercion thread reflects growing third-party-integration demand and the need for a product decision on the tool-call adapter.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (open items today):

P0 / release-blocking

  • #170956 — Windows: slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission error; restarts/updates unreliable. No fix PR linked.
  • #193962 — Fix for SQLite header-probe timeout unreachable on affected installs because package-update runs the installed updater's 10s probe. Source-repro. No fix PR linked.

P1 / crash-loop, data-loss, session-state

  • #144336 — Deferred SIGUSR1 restart fails shutdown ("singleton lifecycle state lost"). Needs live repro.
  • #157255 — Turn claim not released after lane timeout; 90+ min session wedge.
  • #190307 — Gateway restart leaves many agents permanently degraded (admission timeout).
  • #174895 — Live Gateway state owner judged stale; lock reclaimed by second process. Windows.
  • #166641 — web_fetch cold fallback synchronously loads plugins on main thread → liveness stall.
  • #191841 — 2026.10.10 regression: native child reaping unavailable on glibc < 2.31 (RHEL 8/al8); all exec fails.
  • #167472 — Subagent exec approvals fail (missing scope: operator.approvals), fail-closed, no approval card.
  • #192141 — Interrupted-turn continuation drops original user text.

P2 / notable

  • #182891 — Prompt cache never reused (cache read dropped N -> 0).
  • #176187 — Sparse vec0 allocation pushes memory_search past 30s deadline.
  • #194662 — Notification wake invents a sender; main session keeps phantom thread alive.

Assessment: Several of the highest-severity issues have no linked fix PR and require live repro or product decisions, indicating a support bottleneck rather than an engineering one. Notably, #193962 is a meta-bug: the recovery path for a prior fix is itself broken, which is the most dangerous pattern in the set.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • CJK/Chinese search support — #170997 requests a bigram FTS tokenizer (trigram cannot match 2-char queries; unicode61 doesn't segment CJK). Companion issue #173839 on CJK payload prechecks suggests a coherent i18n/APAC push.
  • Rendered Markdown preview in Review files — #128090, 4 👍, fix-shape clear. Low-risk, likely candidate.
  • Android parity — #175826 design-acceptance request for in-chat questions/approvals; PR activity (#195979, #195928, #196300) confirms active Android investment.
  • Per-automation web-search provider — #173518 (closed, product decision pending).
  • Operator recovery tooling — #170562 for stranded requester settle wakes; #165685 machine-readable collector reasons.

Prediction: Near-term releases will likely prioritize (a) CJK search/tokenizer work, (b) Android feature parity, and (c) small Control UI/WebChat polish PRs. Memory/REM exclusion semantics (#172547) is a plausible medium-term item.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points

  • Update/restart reliability is the dominant frustration — users describe requiring "many retries" and hours-long misdiagnoses. #173313 (config get masking sensitive values) reportedly caused a 4+ hour outage verification loop during a Funnel recovery.
  • Silent degradation: sessions wedge for 90+ minutes; agents become "degraded" after restart; crash recovery leaves agents permanently refusing chat.history/models.list.
  • Diagnostic traps: status --deep and status --agent swallow real errors (addressed by PRs #196073, #196081); gateway restart reports failure yet exits 0 (#161158).
  • Deployment friction on Windows (schtasks), Kubernetes (fsGroup), and RHEL 8 (glibc).

Positive signals

  • Maintainers are visibly engaging on high-severity threads (30/27/21 comments), and many PRs are tagged "ready for maintainer look" or carry screenshot/proof evidence.
  • Users file detailed, high-quality reproductions with environment and version data, suggesting a technically invested user base.

Sentiment: Frustrated but engaged. Satisfaction hinges on restart/update reliability; there is clear appetite for fixing the operational substrate before adding features.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or decision-blocked items needing maintainer attention:

Item Age Blocker
#92473 Model fallback notice leaks to user-facing channels ~5 months needs-product-decision
#91931 Preseeded identity files auto-complete bootstrap, delete user BOOTSTRAP.md ~5 months P1, data-loss, needs product decision; fix PR #196302 now open
#137613 Pre-compaction memory flush disabled on CLI backends ~2 months Product decision
#166133 MCP integer→string coercion ~1 month Product decision, 16 comments
#128090 Markdown preview in Review ~2.5 months Fix-shape clear, awaiting maintainer
#173057 Shared agents.defaults.workspace treated as live workspace ~1 month Needs live repro
#151923 Telegram large-media 30s timeout (PR) ~2 months Waiting on maintainer
#178677 Cron jobs blocked on missing creator channel (PR) ~3 weeks Waiting on author, security review required

Priority recommendation: #193962 and #170956 warrant immediate maintainer ownership — they are P0 recovery-path failures with no fix PRs and directly compound user dissatisfaction with updates. #91931 is notable because a fix PR now exists after five months; fast-tracking it would close a long-standing data-loss complaint.

Data source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw, 24h window ending 2026-11-09. Comment/reaction counts reflect items updated in that period; "no fix PR linked" references the clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr label where present.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Snapshot date: 2026-11-10 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant open-source landscape is bifurcating into two camps: mature "Claw-family" runtimes (OpenClaw as reference implementation, plus derivatives Hermes, ZeroClaw, IronClaw) built around agent runtimes, messaging gateways, and plugin ecosystems — and application-layer assistants (QwenPaw) focused on local model runtimes and console UX. The dominant engineering burden across the ecosystem has shifted from feature acquisition to operational reliability: crash recovery, restart/update paths, session-state durability, and security isolation now consume the majority of maintainer attention. Security review is maturing rapidly — ZeroClaw shows a formal S0-severity review pipeline against every open PR, and Hermes/OpenClaw both closed security-boundary bugs this cycle. Local-first inference (MLX, llama.cpp, Ollama) and plugin/marketplace distribution are the two clearest greenfield vectors, while Windows remains the ecosystem's most fragile platform.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h touched) PRs (24h touched) Merge/Close Throughput Release Status Health Score*
OpenClaw 500 (208 closed) 500 (131 merged/closed) Very high, triage-heavy None (no tag in 24h) 6.5 / 10 — high velocity, but P0 restart/update cluster with no fix PRs
Hermes Agent 50 (32 closed) 50 (14 merged/closed) High, converging None (0.23.0 line per reports) 7.5 / 10 — strong close rate, 2 parked P0 needs-decision PRs
IronClaw 0 0 None None N/A — dormant in window
QwenPaw 17 50 (9 merged/closed) High (beta cycle) v2.3.0-beta.3 shipped 7.0 / 10 — active, but beta regressions on packaged builds
ZeroClaw 35 50 Blocked (merge queue stalled) Blocked by CI gate 5.5 / 10 — healthy contributor output, deadlocked pipeline

*Health score is an analyst composite of release cadence, fix velocity, P0/P1 burden, and merge-queue liveness — directional, not a vendor metric.

Key readout: OpenClaw operates at ~10× the raw issue/PR volume of peers — it is the ecosystem's gravity well. QwenPaw is the only project shipping tagged releases this cycle. ZeroClaw is the only project with a fully blocked merge queue, making its high activity deceptive.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers

  • Scale of surface area: 500 issues + 500 PRs touched in 24h vs. 50/50 for Hermes and ZeroClaw. This produces the fastest discovery-to-fix loop in the ecosystem — e.g., PR #196294 cutting knowledge-memory save latency from ~11s to ~2s.
  • Ecosystem gravity: ZeroClaw ships an explicit zeroclaw migrate openclaw-config importer (#12348), and Hermes/ZeroClaw both inherit Claw-family architectural assumptions. OpenClaw is the de facto config and concept standard.
  • Breadth of integrations: Control UI, WebChat, Android, Telegram, Kubernetes, MCP, SQLite-backed memory/search — no peer matches this integration matrix in a single repo.

Technical approach differences

  • SQLite-centric state model (session reclamation, checkpointing, vec0 memory search) — this is OpenClaw's signature bet and also its signature liability (see the P0 session-wedge cluster). Peers like Hermes lean on a REST session API (/api/sessions) and QwenPaw on a local runtime stack.
  • Update/restart subsystem as first-class concern — no peer exposes as much operational tooling (status --deep, gateway restart, openclaw update), and none has as many bugs in it. The #193962 "meta-bug" (the fix for a prior fix is unreachable via the updater) is uniquely an OpenClaw-scale problem.

Community size comparison

  • Issue engagement confirms a larger, more technically invested user base: top threads carry 30/27/21 comments with detailed environment reproductions, versus Hermes' 11/10/9 and QwenPaw's 4-comment ceiling. OpenClaw's users are operating it in production (K8s, RHEL 8, Windows enterprise) — a maturity signal peers have not yet reached.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirement Projects Specific Needs
Trustworthy restart/update & crash recovery OpenClaw (P0: #170956, #193962, #144336), Hermes (resume-provider fix #151956), QwenPaw (#8616 startup AppHang) Restarts must not strand agents; updaters must be able to deliver their own fixes; clean shutdown on SIGUSR1.
Session-state durability / no silent loss OpenClaw (#157255 90-min wedge, #192141 dropped user text), Hermes (#143290 stale /stop drops next turn, #121750 P0 compression archives unseen turns), QwenPaw (#8521 intermittent empty responses) Delivery guarantees over features; fork/reset semantics must be unambiguous across CLI, REST, and desktop.
Security isolation & approval-scope correctness ZeroClaw (S0 batch: #12304–#12311), Hermes (#152125 approver binding, #53674 channel-post bypass), QwenPaw (#8642 MCP policy fencing) Sandbox file access, cross-session attach prevention, approval binding to the requester, fail-closed defaults.
Windows / enterprise-SKU reliability OpenClaw (schtasks, ~5 months of Windows issues), QwenPaw (LTSC startup, long-path, GBK encoding #8234, Chinese-path #8502), Hermes (#152202 non-interactive plugin update) Non-default locales, legacy encodings, frozen-build dependency verification.
Third-party / OpenAI-compatible provider compatibility QwenPaw (#8603 tool-call serialization, #8512/#8615 gateway error formats), Hermes (#149511 pricing coverage), OpenClaw (#166133 MCP integer coercion) Graceful handling of gateway-specific error formats; correct tool-call adapters; per-automation provider routing.
Plugin/marketplace distribution integrity QwenPaw (#8595 metadata missing, #8644 channel activation), Hermes (4 catalog PRs in one day), OpenClaw (MCP adapter demand) Install paths must work via both UI and CLI; plugin lifecycle must be framework-managed.
Local model runtimes QwenPaw (MLX + llama.cpp GPU stack #8647–#8649, Ollama num_ctx #8236), OpenClaw (memory/search tuning) First-party Apple Silicon support, GPU-offload visibility, correct context-window sizing.

Cross-cutting insight: Four of five active projects independently hit the same class of bug — a recovery or continuation path that silently loses data. This is an ecosystem-wide architectural gap, not a per-project defect.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Primary focus Full-stack agent runtime + Control UI + memory Messaging gateway hardening (Telegram-first), plugin catalog Desktop assistant + local model runtime + console UX Secure multi-channel runtime, remote OIDC onboarding
Target users Production operators, K8s/enterprise, self-hosters Group-chat / multi-surface messaging users, plugin authors Desktop/Apple Silicon users, Chinese-locale Windows users Security-sensitive self-hosted daemon operators
Architecture bet SQLite state + gateway + MCP adapter Lease-based room/profile model + REST session contract Frozen desktop builds + MLX/llama.cpp local stack Native Rust channels (XMPP/OMEMO), sandboxed execution
Release rhythm High-velocity maintenance, no tag this cycle Converging toward 0.23 line Fast beta cadence (beta.3 shipped) Blocked pending CI gate
Distinct risk Operational substrate fragility at scale Parked P0 decision-blocked PRs Beta regressions in packaging/dependency path Review-finding security debt + merge deadlock

Notable divergence: ZeroClaw is the only project treating security review as a pre-merge gate producing S0 findings — a materially different engineering culture from OpenClaw's triage-driven model. QwenPaw is the only project investing in first-party local inference, which positions it against OpenClaw's cloud-adapter assumptions.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers

  • Tier 1 — Ecosystem anchor: OpenClaw (500/500, triage-dominant). Mature but carrying operational debt.
  • Tier 2 — Converging stabilizers: Hermes (32 issue closures, Telegram sweep, 14 merges) and QwenPaw (release-shipping beta cycle, 9 merges, 3 first-time contributors). Both are closing faster than they open.
  • Tier 3 — Blocked/dormant: ZeroClaw (contributor output high, merge queue dead — momentum is real but unrealizable) and IronClaw (no activity; likely dormant or pre-launch).

Iterating vs. stabilizing

  • Rapidly iterating: QwenPaw (new MLX/GPU runtime stack in flight, UX polish PRs same-day) and Hermes (plugin catalog expansion — 4 submissions in one day).
  • Stabilizing under load: OpenClaw and Hermes are both in hardening phases — OpenClaw on restarts/sessions, Hermes on Telegram correctness. Neither is adding major features.
  • Stalled: ZeroClaw needs a single dependency decision (#12320) to convert a large backlog of verified fixes into releases. This is the highest-leverage unblock in the ecosystem.

Maturity ranking (composite): OpenClaw > Hermes ≈ QwenPaw > ZeroClaw >> IronClaw. Notably, QwenPaw's release-gating discipline (auto-opened 4-hour cross-platform verification issue #8643) is more mature than its bug volume suggests.

7. Trend Signals (for AI agent developers)

  1. Reliability is the new feature. Across OpenClaw, Hermes, and QwenPaw, users explicitly prioritize delivery guarantees over new capabilities — silent message loss, stale-stop dropping turns, and post-crash wedges are the loudest complaints. Action: design idempotent continuation and explicit "message settled" acknowledgements into any agent loop.
  2. Recovery-path regressions are the most dangerous bug class. OpenClaw's #193962 (fix unreachable via the updater) and ZeroClaw's #12330 (silent local-daemon fallback) show that the path back to health is under-tested. Action: test the updater with the updater; treat failover as a first-class state machine, not a catch block.
  3. Security review is shifting left, pre-merge. ZeroClaw's S0 findings against open PR heads (sandbox dotfile access, approval-scope bypass, cross-session attach) set a new bar. Action: require approval binding to the requesting identity and sandbox-scoped file access by default.
  4. Local-first inference is arriving in the assistant layer. QwenPaw's MLX/llama.cpp/GPU-control stack and Ollama num_ctx fix signal that desktop assistants will own their inference runtime. Action: abstract model backends early; do not hard-code cloud adapter assumptions.
  5. Platform parity is a trust issue, not a nicety. Windows (schtasks, long paths, GBK), RHEL 8 (glibc), iPhone Safari (requestIdleCallback), and Linux translucency all generate outsized frustration. Action: treat non-default locale/encoding and frozen-build environments as tier-1 test targets.
  6. Ecosystem interop is consolidating around OpenClaw conventions. ZeroClaw's migration importer and shared Claw-family config concepts suggest a de facto standard is forming. Action: for new entrants, align config/session semantics with OpenClaw to inherit tooling and migrate-in paths.
  7. Plugin marketplaces are the next reliability frontier. Install-path failures (#8595), frozen-build activation regressions (#8644), and framework-managed lifecycle PRs (#8431) all point the same way. Action: design plugin dependency verification and lifecycle management before scaling a catalog.

Bottom line for decision-makers: OpenClaw is the ecosystem's reference implementation and should be tracked as the compatibility baseline; Hermes and QwenPaw are the healthiest active bets for messaging-gateway and desktop/local-runtime use cases respectively; ZeroClaw carries the strongest security posture but needs its CI gate resolved before it can ship; IronClaw shows no signal this cycle. The defining 2026 engineering problem is operational trust — restarts, recovery, and delivery guarantees — not feature breadth.

Peer Project Reports

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent — Project Digest

Date: 2026-11-10 | Repo: NousResearch/hermes-agent

1. Today's Overview

Hermes Agent shows high activity with net-positive throughput: 50 issues and 50 PRs touched in the last 24h, balanced toward closure (32 issues closed vs. 18 open/active; 14 PRs merged/closed vs. 36 open). No new releases were cut, but the merge queue is heavily oriented toward Telegram platform hardening — fallback network paths, duplicate-send prevention, forum-topic isolation, and approval-scope security fixes — suggesting a sustained stabilization push on the messaging gateway ahead of a possible tagged release. Open work is dominated by P2 bugs across the gateway, desktop shell, and session state, with several long-lived Telegram issues from July–September finally closing today. Overall project health reads active and converging, though a small cluster of P0/needs-decision compression and session-state PRs remains parked.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. (Latest known line in the wild is v0.22.2 stable and v0.23.0 per issue reports; no tag published 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-10.)

3. Project Progress

14 PRs merged/closed today. Notable closed items:

PR What it closed Impact
#152262 Group Chat turns queued behind a busy profile now keep their room lease and settle Fixes silent reply discard ("indeterminate") when multiple members share a profile
#152125 approvals.approvers: [] binds to real sender + one admin scope on every surface Security hardening — closes gap where non-requesters could approve risky commands
#142512 Hosted-room terminal settle alive across plain lease expiry Fixes load-sensitive flaky test / wedged "running" state

Issue closures (32 total) were overwhelmingly Telegram-related: flood-control/typing cooldown (#99643, #107612), duplicate-send on network error (#64238), webhook re-registration (#141397), channel-post gating (#53674), fork/topic routing (#58850, #36992, #65202), and redaction false-positives (#145664) — a broad Telegram reliability and correctness sweep.

Still open and advancing: profile provisioning refactor (#149075), Bots room-view delta reads (#149210), and pricing coverage for OpenCode Zen routes (#149511).

4. Community Hot Topics

Rank Item Comments Signal
1 #141988 — process_manage TypeError paging background output 11 Regression blocking log retrieval on macOS; long-running (since 10-20)
2 #145183 — Desktop translucent on Linux, no UI toggle 10 (👍1) UI/UX mismatch; effect cannot be disabled
3 #142064 — /api/sessions omits _reset_from 9 REST client contract inconsistency (fork vs. /new mislabeled)
4 #142488 — model switch crash on tuple moved 8 Desktop model-switch blocker for profile-following sessions
5 #143290 — stale /stop interrupts next turn 8 Data-loss class: message silently dropped

Underlying needs analysis: The hottest threads cluster around session-state correctness (fork semantics, reset markers, stale stop signals) and platform parity (desktop settings not reflecting backend capability). Users are integrating via REST clients and desktop UI, not just the CLI — the /api/sessions contract and desktop Settings parity are becoming first-class concerns.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity:

P1 / Data-loss & security

  • #143290 (P2 but data-loss impact) — POST /v1/runs/{id}/stop on a just-finished run interrupts the next turn; new message silently dropped. No fix PR visible.
  • #53674 — Telegram channel posts bypass allowed_chats/require_mention, treated as DMs — CLOSED today (security boundary fix landed).
  • #151762 — Discord DM-only admin can approve group approval via buttons — CLOSED today; #152125 merged as the fix.

P2 / Functional regressions

  • #141988 — process_manage TypeError: slice indices must be integers — open, 11 comments, no fix PR yet (oldest high-traffic open bug).
  • #145183 — Linux desktop translucency with hidden Settings toggle — open.
  • #142488 — Desktop model switch crash (moved rename-map shadowed) — open.
  • #142064 — /api/sessions missing _reset_from — open.
  • #152148 — Fresh Telegram DM topics invisible/unopenable — open (new today, cause/upstream tagged).
  • #148538 — iPhone Safari: requestIdleCallback undefined, pages fail to render — open.

Fix PRs in flight (good stability signal):

  • #151833, #151801, #151930, #151772 — a coherent Telegram fallback/duplicate-send/forum-isolation patchset (all ci-reviewed).
  • #151956 — resumed chats keep custom provider (fixes #132648).
  • #152230 — errors name the actual cause (better diagnostics).

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Plugin catalog expansion is the dominant feature vector: #151013 (hermes-audio-api, OpenAI-compatible audio endpoints), #151014 (hermes-fal-video, three FAL video tools + bundled skill), #152195 (borrowed-hands, Xcode compile offload from cloud Hermes), #152201 (FollowThrough commitments plugin). All require Hermes ≥0.23.0 — suggests 0.23 is the target release line for catalog-compatible plugins.
  • Bots/Group Chat architecture step 2 in #149210 — log-delta room views + groups.changed push; roadmap artifact linked in PR.
  • Dismissible todo/previous-tasks UI requested in #127429 (open, 8 comments).
  • Pricing coverage for OpenCode Zen in #149511.

Prediction: Next release will emphasize Telegram gateway reliability + plugin catalog additions; Bots architecture improvements are staged for a follow-on.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • "Silent loss" is the recurring theme — dropped messages after stale /stop, archived unseen turns under compression (#121750, P0), undelivered send_path_degraded replies (#123898). Users prioritize delivery guarantees over new features.
  • Platform parity friction: Linux users stuck with unwanted translucency; iPhone Safari route failures; Windows non-interactive plugins update blocked (#152202).
  • Cross-surface contract drift: REST clients misrender forks due to missing _reset_from; TUI/desktop disagreement on provider on resume.

Satisfaction signals: Multiple long-standing Telegram bugs and a security-boundary issue (#53674) closed with linked fixes — strong evidence maintainers are responsive to well-tagged reports. Community plugin authors actively submitting (4 catalog PRs today), indicating a healthy extension ecosystem.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention (old, high-comment, or P0/needs-decision):

  • 🔴 #121750 — P0, needs-decision, compression archives unseen turns (open since 2026-09-24, 47 days). Data-loss risk.
  • 🔴 #132948 — P0, needs-decision, webui-ng YOLO resume / failure_reason / fork prompt races (open since 10-04).
  • 🟠 #141988 — 11 comments, 21 days open, no fix PR — top open bug by engagement.
  • 🟠 #127429 — dismiss/clear previous-tasks UI, 42 days open.
  • 🟠 #142064 — /api/sessions contract gap, 21 days open.
  • 🟡 #152202 — non-interactive plugins update (new, but blocks SSH/CI automation workflows).

Health verdict: Project is actively maintained with a strong close rate and a clear Telegram-focused fix wave. The main risk is the two parked P0 needs-decision PRs related to session state and compression — these are decision-blocked, not implementation-blocked, and warrant maintainer resolution before the next tagged release.

Generated from GitHub activity 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-10. All counts per provided dataset.

IronClaw — nearai/ironclaw

No activity in the last 24 hours.

QwenPaw — agentscope-ai/QwenPaw

QwenPaw Project Digest — 2026-11-10

1. Today's Overview

QwenPaw is in an active beta stabilization cycle following the v2.3.0-beta.3 release. Activity remains very high: 50 PRs and 17 issues were updated in the last 24h, including 9 merged/closed PRs. The dominant theme is the new "QwenPaw Local" model-runtime stack (llama.cpp GPU controls, managed MLX), split across three stacked PRs (#8649 → #8647 → #8648). Alongside new features, a cluster of Windows-specific packaging and channel-plugin activation bugs continues to surface in the 2.3.0 betas, and memory/search performance issues are being addressed by external contributors. Overall project health is good—active maintainer review, rapid issue triage, and healthy first-time-contributor participation—though the volume of beta regressions suggests the 2.3.0 GA release may need additional hardening time.

2. Releases

v2.3.0-beta.3 (release page)

Changes:

  • docs(memory): Added separate bilingual blogs for multimodal memory and Memory Tags (#8506)
  • fix(channels): Resolved desktop plugin installation and repair failures (PR referenced in release notes)

Notes:

  • This is a beta release; no explicit breaking changes or migration notes were published in the changelog.
  • A Release Duty installation-verification issue (#8643) was auto-opened with a 4-hour verification deadline across platforms; this is a good signal of mature release gating.
  • Caution for upgraders: beta.3 is generating its own new regression reports (see §5), notably channel-plugin activation failures on packaged Desktop builds (#8644). Users on stable 2.2.2 may want to wait for beta.4 or GA.

3. Project Progress

Nine PRs were merged/closed in the last 24h, concentrated on test infrastructure, CI reliability, and cleanup:

PR Type Summary
#8639 test fix Fixed BOM decoding in dependency installation test
#8640 test fix Fixed Windows permission (0600) and UTF-8 BOM assertions — improves cross-platform CI determinism
#8641 CI fix Extended macOS desktop build timeout to 90 minutes — likely unblocks slow macOS packaging pipeline
#8645 feature (superseded) Closed in favor of the re-split MLX stack (#8647/#8648/#8649)

Significant in-flight work advanced today (high comment/update activity):

  • Local model runtime overhaul — the three stacked PRs #8649 (llama.cpp GPU + auto-update), #8647 (managed MLX), #8648 (console controls) form a coherent feature set and are likely the headline of the next release.
  • Security fix in MCP driver policy publication — #8642 fences stale policy publication so a slow MCP reload cannot restore a revoked allow-policy. This is a meaningful access-control correctness fix.
  • Provider compatibility fixes — #8512 (gateway status-code extraction) and #8615 (recognizing gateway context-overflow 400s) improve robustness against third-party OpenAI-compatible gateways.
  • Memory search performance — #8623 (first-time contributor) eliminates duplicate turn-boundary resolution.

4. Community Hot Topics

The most-discussed items (by comment count) reveal three underlying community needs: beta reliability on Windows, plugin ecosystem integrity, and agent UX transparency.

  1. #8595 — Plugin install fails: "No package metadata was found" for qwenpaw-creator (4 comments, OPEN) Need: The official plugin install path is broken via both UI and CLI. This undermines the plugin marketplace as a distribution channel — users cannot reliably install first-party extensions.

  2. #8521 — Missing responses in chat + Ctrl+C copy requires multiple presses + new UI slower (4 comments, OPEN) Need: A compound UX regression report: reliability of chat output, clipboard behavior across Chrome/Edge, and a request to toggle back to the old UI. Signals dissatisfaction with the 2.x console redesign and possible rendering/streaming issues.

  3. #8627 — Checkpoint service fails on Git long-path + WeChat channel stuck at DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS (2 comments, OPEN) Need: Windows long-path environment handling and opaque dependency-verification states. Users need actionable diagnostics rather than ambiguous status codes.

  4. #8616 — 2.3.0-beta.1 fails to start on Windows 11 IoT LTSC, AppHang (2 comments, OPEN) Need: Regression relative to 2.2.2 on the same machine — a hard startup blocker for enterprise LTSC deployments.

  5. MLX/GPU feature stack (#8646 issue + PRs #8647/#8648/#8649) — Apple Silicon users want first-party MLX support and visibility into GPU offload; the maintainer-authored PR stack shows this is being actively delivered.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (user impact × breadth), with fix status:

Critical

  • #8616 — Desktop 2.3.0-beta.1 will not start on Windows 11 IoT LTSC ("path not found" → AppHang) — Regression vs. 2.2.2. Hard blocker; no fix PR identified yet.
  • #8644 — All channel plugins (feishu, wechat, yuanbao) fail to activate on packaged Desktop builds (2.3.0b3) — AttributeError in validate_runtime_identity reading supported_tags from DependencyReadEvidence. This is a regression in the just-released beta.3 and affects every messaging integration on frozen builds. Highest-priority fix candidate.

High

  • #8595 — Plugin install fails with "No package metadata was found" — Blocks plugin installation entirely; note the beta.3 changelog claims a channels/plugin-install fix, so verify whether this persists.
  • #8627 — Checkpoint service fails on Git long-path + WeChat channel stuck at DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS — Windows environment edge case; related dependency-verification logic overlaps with #8644/#8553.
  • #8603 — run_code invoked with empty arguments on custom OpenAI-compatible providers — Every tool call rejected with 'code' is a required property on user-defined providers (kimi, k3.1-pro). Breaks a core agent capability for third-party model users.
  • #8629 — Oversized historical image re-sent every model call; stripped retry retains misleading "Image loaded" text — Wastes tokens/quota and misleads users about request state.

Medium

  • #8619 — Repeated turn boundary queries for same search hits — Performance bug; fix PR exists: #8623.
  • #8620 — SQLite errors masked as TimeoutError on elapsed search deadline — Diagnostic quality issue in MemorySpace.search.
  • #8521 — Intermittent empty chat responses + Ctrl+C copy failures — Reproduction unclear; could be model-side or UI-side.

Fixed / Closed today

  • #8585 — recall_history broken on Windows: \\?\ extended-length path breaks SQLite read-only URI — ✅ CLOSED
  • #8553 — QQ channel fails with DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED when hub plugin lacks dependency env — ✅ CLOSED
  • #8502 — Desktop HTML preview "open in browser" broken for Chinese paths — ✅ CLOSED

Stability assessment: The 2.3.0 beta line has a recurring theme — packaged/frozen Desktop builds and dependency-environment verification are fragile (see #8644, #8627, #8553, #8616). Maintainers appear to be fixing these reactively per-beta; a dedicated audit of the frozen-build identity/dependency path would likely prevent further regressions before GA.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Request Issue Likelihood / Signal
Managed MLX engine + GPU controls for QwenPaw Local (Apple Silicon) #8646 Very high — already implemented in the maintainer PR stack #8647/#8648/#8649. Expect in next beta.
UX: consistent visual style for thinking blocks vs. tool cards; stop left-edge jumping #8650 Medium — small, well-scoped UI polish; fits a patch release.
UX: "execution-type" tool calls should show human-readable intent #8612 High, already in flight — #8638 adds an optional title param to execute_shell_command (also fixes a validation issue).
Browser tab title should reflect current session name #8605 Medium — simple console change; plausible near-term.
Quote assistant response selections into follow-up drafts (PR #8609) Implemented in PR; likely next release.
UI toggle to revert to the old console layout (implicit in #8521) #8521 Low/uncertain — historically maintainers rarely ship dual-UI modes; more likely they address specific friction (model switching).

Prediction for v2.3.0 GA / beta.4: Local MLX + GPU controls, shell-card intent titles, quote-to-draft, and the memory-search performance fix are the strongest candidates. UX consistency (#8650) is plausible as a fast-follow.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Windows is the dominant friction surface. Startup failures on LTSC (#8616), long-path/checkpoint issues (#8627), extended-path SQLite bugs (#8585, now fixed), and Chinese-path HTML preview failures (#8502, now fixed) all cluster on Windows configurations — especially non-default locales and enterprise SKUs.
  • Plugin/channel ecosystem reliability. Multiple independent reports (#8595, #8644, #8553, #8627) show plugin installation and channel activation are the least stable subsystem in 2.3.x betas.
  • New console UX dissatisfaction. Users report the redesigned UI feels slower and less information-dense than the old one, with specific complaints about model switching ergonomics and per-press clipboard failures (#8521). Tool-card readability is a recurring theme (#8612, #8650).
  • Third-party provider compatibility. Users running custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (kimi, gateways like Strata) hit broken tool-call serialization (#8603) and unrecognized gateway error formats (#8512, #8615).

Positive signals:

  • Users are filing high-quality, well-scoped bug reports with environment details and reproduction steps, which correlates with maintainer responsiveness (19 of 20 top PRs updated today).
  • Three first-time-contributor PRs are active (#8606 docs dead-link fix, #8623 memory perf, #8642 MCP policy fencing) — a healthy sign of community investment.
  • Apple Silicon users are engaged and their top request (MLX) is being delivered by the maintainer team, which should convert to satisfaction.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention (older or lower-visibility but consequential):

  1. #8234 — fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 instead of silently dropping bytes in read/edit/grep — Open since 2026-10-14 (~27 days). Addresses silent data loss for Chinese Windows users' legacy text files. High user value for a large locale segment; has been "Under Review" for weeks.
  2. #8236 — fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default — Open since 2026-10-14. Local Ollama users get incorrect context-window assumptions, causing truncation or overflow errors. Directly relevant to the local-models push; should be coordinated with the #8647–#8649 stack.
  3. #8170 — fix(console): tolerate DOM-mutation render errors + chunk-error retry (rebased #7889) — Open since 2026-10-10 (~31 days), already rebased once. Render-error tolerance plausibly relates to the intermittent UI failures in #8521; worth prioritizing given user complaints about console stability.
  4. #8431 — feat: convert local Whisper into an SDK plugin with framework-managed lifecycle — Large (XXXL) PR open since 2026-10-26; touches plugin lifecycle, which is exactly the subsystem generating the most beta bugs (#8644, #8553). Needs architectural review before it compounds with the plugin-dependency refactor.
  5. #8606 — docs: fix 5 dead external links — First-time contributor, small and low-risk; quick merge would be a good onboarding signal.

Maintainer recommendation: Prioritize (a) the #8644 packaged-build channel-activation regression as a beta.3 hotfix, (b) merging the long-pending #8234/#8236 localization/local-model fixes, and (c) a focused audit of the frozen-build dependency-verification path to stop the recurring Windows beta regressions before GA.

Data source: github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw, activity window 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-10. All links point to the corresponding GitHub issue/PR pages.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-10

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw is in a blocked-release state: Issue #12320 reports that RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2 / bundled SQLite 3.53.2) fails the Security job on every CI run, which cascades into CI Required Gate failure — meaning no PR can merge and the merge queue is stalled. Activity remains high (35 issues and 50 PRs touched in 24h) but is heavily skewed toward review findings: a single reviewer (IftekharUddin) filed a batch of S0 security findings against open PR heads (#12304–#12312, #12305, #12306, #12309, #12310, #12311) and tidux landed a large zerocode OIDC login PR (#12317) with a cluster of follow-up issues (#12331–#12340). No releases were cut, consistent with the blocked gate. Net assessment: healthy contributor throughput, degraded merge health due to a CI blocker plus several critical pre-merge security findings.

2. Releases

None in this window. Note for planning: all release-tagged work is currently gated behind #12320.

3. Project Progress

Merged/closed PRs today:

  • #12348 (closed, XL) — feat(migrate): import OpenClaw config, agents, and workspaces: adds zeroclaw migrate openclaw-config, mapping providers, fallback chains, and agents (balanced risk preset). Significant ecosystem-interop feature.
  • #11933 (closed, XS) — fix(web): keep the chat header on screen in narrow layouts: responsive fix for mobile chat.
  • #11920 (closed, XS) — feat(web): toggle to keep the live Thinking box collapsed (closes #11919): UX improvement for reasoning models.
  • #12342 (closed, XS) — docs: bounded runtime placement exception for zerocode OIDC (#12317), unblocking that feature's merge contract.

Closed issues: #10359 (audit-log hash-chain poisoning — pre-existing, now closed), #11009 (alias rename not cascading permission profiles), #12064 (Discord peer-bot approval bypass), #12087 (tool toggle double-save), #11952 (--prefixed relative data dir), #12312 (OIDC discovery endpoint policy gap), #11919 (Thinking box).

4. Community Hot Topics

  1. Issue #12320 — CI security gate failure (S1, 3 comments). The single highest-leverage thread: every release and merge depends on resolving the RUSTSEC advisory. Needs either a dependency bump or a scoped, documented advisory exception.
  2. PR #12317 — feat(zerocode): pairing-free OIDC login and saved remote credentials (XL). Attracted 10+ follow-up issues (#12330–#12340) — proof of high interest in frictionless remote onboarding, but also of review load: the PR head has known rough edges (ledger actor double-prefix, smoke-test ordering, cert-without-CA semantics, credential pruning).
  3. PR #11847 — native Rust XMPP with optional OMEMO (XL, high risk) and companion #12015 (ChaCha20Poly1305 unification) and #12319 (duplicate-crate allowances). Community push for channel breadth; this is one of the largest open feature trains.
  4. PR #12244 — scoped dashboard chat through core RPC (XL, do-not-merge, blocked). Long-running core architecture PR.

Underlying needs: (a) an unblocked release pipeline, (b) lower-friction remote login, (c) broader/more modern channel support, (d) consolidation of duplicated crypto/dependency surfaces.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (all filed/updated 2026-11-09 unless noted):

  • S1 / workflow-blocking: #12320 — RUSTSEC-2026-0459 fails Security job on every build; merge queue and release are deadlocked. No fix PR yet.
  • S0 security (review findings against open PR heads; fix = revise the PR before merge):
    • #12311 — macOS Seatbelt profile grants sandboxed commands read access to all home dotfiles incl. ~/.zeroclaw (PR #12150).
    • #12310 — MCP config-control bridge grants model unrestricted config writes with no approval (PR #12275).
    • #12309 — sessions_prompt target scoping unenforced; PR head doesn't compile (PR #12258).
    • #12308 — session delete/TTL leaves transcripts and payloads readable; no erasure path.
    • #12307 — gateway sessions lose gw_ namespace → cross-session attach by paired callers.
    • #12306 — Matrix Goal parent turns bypass effort_routing allowlist (cloud_escalation = never).
    • #12305 — daemon-wide cost-limit override approvable by any allowlisted peer on non-Telegram channels.
    • #12304 — colony channel replies leak operator messages to external members (PR #11560).
  • S2: #12330 — zerocode silently falls back to local daemon when zerocode-config.toml is unreadable/unparseable (risk of wrong-endpoint connections); #12325 — docs canonical URLs point at a release dir, so every release reshuffles SEO URLs.
  • S3: #12347 — zerocode config writers can lose concurrent updates (read-modify-write, no lock); #12326 and #12324 — docs 404s for pruned versions and indexable rustdoc/404 pages.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Remote access without pairing ceremony — #12317's OIDC self-service device certificate bootstrap, gated behind operator opt-in per #12337. Strong candidate for v0.9.0 once #12320 clears.
  • Channel breadth & security — XMPP/OMEMO (#11847), owner notifications for unauthorized inbound messages (PR #12346), Matrix routing hardening (#12306).
  • Migration/interop — OpenClaw import (#12348, already closed).
  • Web UX — voice settings for paired devices (PR #12269), collapsed Thinking toggle (#11919, done), narrow-layout fixes (#11933, done).
  • Credential hygiene — pruning superseded OIDC credential generations (#12339) and defining cert-without-CA semantics (#12338).

Prediction: next release will be dominated by security hardening (sandbox, session isolation, approval paths), zerocode OIDC onboarding, and channel work — contingent entirely on #12320.

7. User Feedback Summary

  • Frustration: release/CI blockage (#12320) is the loudest signal — nothing can land; contributors are producing verified fixes with nowhere to merge.
  • Security-sensitive users (self-hosted/daemon operators) are surfacing concrete isolation concerns: sandbox file access, cross-session attach, group-chat approval abuse, and message leakage. These read as real deployment pain, not theoretical.
  • Mobile/web users: satisfied with responsive and UX fixes (#11933, #11920), indicating active dashboard usage on phones.
  • Onboarding friction: zerocode users want pairing-free login and are willing to accept opt-in defaults (#12337); the volume of follow-ups shows the feature is wanted but the current head is not production-ready.
  • Silent-failure anxiety: #12330 (config parse failure → local daemon fallback) and #12347 (lost config writes) are the kind of subtle degradations that erode trust in the TUI client.

8. Backlog Watch

  • PR #11868 (open since 2026-10-19, needs-maintainer-review) — repeated-call suppression before dispatch; blocks related #11911 and has companion docs PR #12265 awaiting action.
  • PR #11317 (open since 2026-10-01, XS docs) — bounded plugin webhook RPC placement exception; a month-old one-row docs PR still unreviewed.
  • PR #11847 (open since 2026-10-19, XL, needs-maintainer-review) — XMPP channel train; needs review bandwidth to avoid bit-rot against master.
  • PR #12244 (blocked, do-not-merge) — dashboard chat via core RPC; high risk and long-lived, at risk of conflict churn.
  • Issue #12320 — not old, but the most urgent: it is the keystone blocking the entire merge queue and next release.

All links reference github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw. Data snapshot: 2026-11-09/10 activity window.

横向对比

跨项目对比报告 — AI 基础设施生态

摘要日期：2026-11-10

1. 生态概览

今日的动态印证了一个双层基础设施格局：服务引擎（vLLM、SGLang）正处于硬件适配的堑壕战之中——SM120/GB10 消费级 Blackwell 与 MI355X/MI450 如今消耗了大部分 issue 和 PR 带宽，且正确性回归（静默空补全、内核输出静默损坏）的数量已超过功能开发。本地/边缘层（llama.cpp、Ollama、Unsloth） 迭代速度很快，但正沿后端（Metal、Vulkan、SYCL、ROCm、OpenCL、XDNA）走向碎片化，可复现性与 KV 缓存正确性成为反复出现的薄弱环节。网关层（LiteLLM） 正围绕计量正确性进行整合——一批已关闭的预算/限流绕过缺陷，加上原生 Rust 后端的 /v1/messages 路径，表明计费准确性已成为主要竞争轴。在所有层级中，投机解码正成熟为默认的吞吐量杠杆，同时也在产生最大的一簇正确性回归（EAGLE/MTP/DFlash/DFlash2/DSpine 分歧、TP>1 时接受率崩塌）。值得注意的是：过去 24 小时内 vLLM、SGLang 或 Unsloth 均无发布——今日的工作是集成与缺陷修复，而非发版。

谁领先： vLLM 在广度上领先（Kimi K3.1、MiniMax M3、Nemotron-H、DeepSeek-V4.1），但在新硬件上承载了最多的模型专属回归。llama.cpp 在长尾架构支持上领先（Gemma 4 音频、DFLASH2/DSpine、Granite NVFP4），并且是新 drafter 格式事实上的参考实现。Unsloth 在 Qwen3.5/3.6 与 Gemma 4 推理加速 上意外位居第二，正从训练侧向服务引擎的领地渗透。LiteLLM 是唯一在添加云厂商模型对齐（Fable 5.2 于 Vertex/Bedrock）的项目——它的竞赛发生在 API 形态层，而非内核层。Ollama 的新模型覆盖面最窄，且仍受制于 Qwen3.5 MoE 并行（numParallel=1）。

集中度解读： 可见三场不同的战役。(a) AMD 已成为一等性能目标——SGLang 拥有最深的 MI355X/MI450 内核流水线（DSA top-k、ring all-reduce、AITER 汇编 MLA）；vLLM 正以 ROCm AITER MLA 追赶（但遭遇了一个已关闭的严重静默损坏缺陷 #66141）。(b) KV 缓存容量是普遍瓶颈——vLLM 通过工作区调优回收，Unsloth 通过可增长分配，SGLang 通过 supernode 共享；Ollama 的 Vulkan prompt 缓存 30× 回归是警示性的反例。(c) 解码图正从训练框架向外扩散——Unsloth 默认开启的 CUDA 图在 T4 上带来 2–8×，是本摘要集中最大的头条吞吐量声明，且它直接与服务引擎争夺“小模型、高吞吐”用例。

5. 层级定位

层级 项目 核心功能 本周战略信号
服务引擎（数据中心） vLLM、SGLang 高吞吐、多 GPU、PagedAttention 级服务；分离式 prefill/decode（PD）、TP/PP/DP 两者均受制于硬件适配：SM120/GB10 与 MI 侧缺口占主导。功能迭代速度是后端 bring-up 的下游。差异化正转向正确性保障（确定性标志、消除静默失败），而非原始吞吐量。
本地 / 边缘运行时 llama.cpp、Ollama 单节点/消费级服务、GGUF 量化、多后端可移植性（Metal/CUDA/Vulkan/SYCL/OpenCL/NPU） llama.cpp 是后端可移植性领先者但正碎片化（每天 18 个构建横跨 10 个后端）；Ollama 是整合者/分发层，押注 OpenAI 兼容与 Docker 捆绑的 MLX/Vulkan。两者均面临 KV 缓存正确性债务（#11970、#30961）。
网关 / 控制平面 LiteLLM 路由、限流、预算、成本核算、提供商归一化、PII 护栏 网关正成为计量与策略执行点——本周的 issue 簇（5 个高危预算/限流绕过，均已关闭）证明该层仍在加固。原生 Rust /v1/messages（7 个 PR 的栈）是热路径的基础设施语言迁移。
微调 → 服务桥梁 Unsloth SFT/RL 微调，随后通过 FastModel.generate() 与 Studio 进行本地服务 Unsloth 正纵向向上整合：解码 CUDA 图、可增长 KV、OpenAI 兼容的 Studio 网关。对于 Qwen/Llama/Gemma 级工作负载，它如今已是可信的单机服务引擎替代方案。训练侧正确性（CPU 评估损失 #17291）是当前的缺口。

采购视角： vLLM/SGLang = 横向扩展的多租户服务；llama.cpp = 最大硬件可移植性与模型广度；Ollama = 开发者体验与分发；LiteLLM = 多提供商治理与成本控制；Unsloth = 一站式微调后服务。这些互补而非可替代——有意思的重叠在于 Unsloth 对本地服务引擎，以及 LiteLLM 对原生提供商 SDK。

6. 趋势信号

1. 静默正确性失败是新的可用性风险。 本周两个 CRITICAL 级 issue 返回HTTP 200 但内容错误：vLLM 的 NVFP4 MoE 在 SM120 上空补全（#51525，content: null + finish_reason: length）以及已关闭但待验证的 ROCm AITER MLA 不相关输出（#66141）。结合 llama.cpp 的投机解码 temp-0 分歧（#31472）与 SGLang 可破坏的 prefill CUDA 图分歧（#49133），信息很明确：输出校验必须成为服务栈的一部分，而不是应用的假设。

2. 投机解码既是吞吐量默认项，也是正确性前沿。 今天每个项目都触及了它——vLLM（EAGLE/MTP 前缀缓存块丢弃，30–40% 批损失；DFlash TP>1 崩塌）、SGLang（EAGLE 重复惩罚偏斜修复）、llama.cpp（DFLASH2/DSpine、temp-0 分歧）、Unsloth（解码图）。运行对可复现性敏感的评估或确定性 agent 的开发者应禁用投机解码或锁定版本，直到各项目的修复矩阵落地。

3. AMD 不再是次要目标——它是共同一等公民。 SGLang 有密集的 MI355X/MI450 PR 流；vLLM 有 MI355X 性能追踪器与“MonoKernel”提案（#60904）；llama.cpp 与 Ollama 承载着持续的 ROCm/Vulkan 问题（RDNA AWQ 慢 2.5×、gfx1151 NaN、VRAM 误报）。集群标准化应将 ROCm 视为一个独立的、重度依赖版本锁定的环境——而非 CUDA 路径的直接替代。

4. 消费级 Blackwell（SM120/GB10）在两个服务引擎上开箱即属损坏层级。 vLLM（CUDA 图失败、静默空补全）与 SGLang（CUDA 13 wheel 安装失败；因移除 DSV4.1 DeepGEMM 门控导致约 8× prefill 回归，#49173）独立证实 SM120 当前对量化 MoE 或长上下文尚未生产就绪。Blackwell 数据中心（SM100/SM90）没问题；消费级 SKU 才是缺口。

5. 网关正成为受审计的控制平面。 LiteLLM 的五个已关闭高危预算/限流绕过（预留路径之外的项目预算、陈旧重置将支出清零、已删除团队密钥的认证缓存残留、按团队模型限制减半）加上预先宣布的 2.0.0 空 models 语义变更，意味着 agent/应用开发者应：升级后审计限额，在链式代理拓扑中对照提供商账单核对流式用量（#36114），并在弃用窗口关闭前显式枚举允许的模型。

6. OpenAI 兼容是入场券，结构化输出才是创新。 llama.cpp 的顶层 json_schema 修复（b12229）、Ollama 的 /v1/models 空数组变更与截断转发，以及 Unsloth Studio 的自定义端点网关，都汇聚于 OpenAI 线格式兼容。下一步是模式强制的结构化生成——llama.cpp 的 token 感知聊天解析（#29307/#31978）正将 <think>/工具调用解析从客户端字符串匹配迁移到服务端发出的字段。为 agent 框架规划这一迁移。

7. 下周关注：

  • vLLM： Marlin→Humming 迁移是否能以同等性能落地；DeepSeek-V4.1 的 SM120 CUDA 图修复。
  • SGLang： v0.5.22→v0.5.23 解码回归的解决（对 DeepSeek-V4.1 交互式 agent 至关重要）；MI450 all-reduce 落地。
  • llama.cpp： KV 缓存截断（#11970）与 prompt 缓存恢复（#30961）——两者均为长期 HIGH 且影响多轮正确性。
  • Ollama： 在 v0.40.16-rc0 与 #19632 VRAM 核算修复之后趋于稳定——这是本周期升级的最强理由。
  • LiteLLM： 2.0.0 迁移工具；面向 Anthropic 协议客户端的原生 /v1/messages 栈完成。
  • Unsloth： 带确定性验证的解码图 GA；可增长 KV 发布；Studio 是成熟为可信的 agent 路由网关，还是仍停留在开发工具。

  10. 低 — [Issue #59988] --api-server-count > 1：Prometheus 指标在首个请求前为空。链接
  11. 低 — [PR #66489] ChatCompletionRequest 中的空 messages 列表现在在验证阶段被拒绝（此前在生成后返回 HTTP 500）。链接

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 按硬件锁定你的技术栈。 SM120/Blackwell 消费级用户（RTX 50xx、RTX PRO 6000）在量化 MoE 和 DeepSeek-V4.1 上仍面临静默空补全和 CUDA graph 失败。请验证输出内容，而不仅仅是 HTTP 200 — 这些失败返回 finish_reason: length 和 null 内容，而非错误。
  • 新 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 部署上的长上下文需要显式截断测试 — 目前 GB10 上超过约 2K token 的内容可能被静默忽略（#62776）。
  • 前缀缓存 + 投机解码在混合注意力模型上仍是吞吐陷阱（#53670、#51771）：前缀复用负载下预计批吞吐损失 30–40%；在 #52244 落地前，请禁用投机解码或锁定到不含该末块丢弃回归的版本。
  • 边缘场景下准入控制很重要。 KV 饱和的服务器通过重试风暴使解码 TPOT 膨胀约 2.3 倍（#64460）— 请在前端使用队列感知的负载均衡，而非简单的轮询。
  • 小型运维收益可期： FlashInfer 工作区调优可在消费级 GPU 上恢复约 20% 的 KV 容量；新的 VLLM_TRITON_SYNC_AUTOTUNE_TP 标志可稳定 TP rank 内核选择，适合对可复现性敏感的工作负载。
  • RL/微调流水线： 关注 Direct Weight Reload RFC（#54477）和 Load Plan API（#64418）— 两者都旨在消除权重更新中与重载相关的静默陈旧问题。
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang 摘要 — 2026-11-10

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但 issue 活动主要由 CI/runner 不稳定以及一组 SM120（消费级 Blackwell / GB10）覆盖缺口主导，这些缺口正在导致 prefill 和 attention 后端回归。在性能方面，AMD 贡献者继续为 MI355X/MI450 落地 DSA/MLA 和 all-reduce kernel 工作，同时有报告称 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 上出现新的 SM90 decode 回归（v0.5.22 → v0.5.23）。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时内无。注意 issue #49336 指出 v0.5.22（baa9befa38）与 v0.5.23（297e54fd10）之间引入的性能回归——见稳定性部分。

  • Issue #49336 — 未报告 API/配置破坏，但存在与 v0.5.23 升级相关的 decode 延迟回归。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • DeepSeek 图像聊天路由（sgl-router）： PR #48937 通过 ChatFormatter::encode_multimodal_request 为多模态 DeepSeek 聊天添加前缀缓存感知路由（依赖 #46562）。PR #48937
  • Clover-35B-A3B-Preview（Diffuspace）： PR #46927 添加原生 serving 以及使用共享模型进行并行 draft 生成和 AR 验证的自推测解码。PR #46927
  • 寒武纪 MLU 后端： Roadmap issue #45615 提议 MLU 后端。Issue #45615
  • AMD gfx1250（MI45x）AITER 固定： Issue #47562 跟踪针对 gfx1250 的独立 AITER 固定版本的手动验证，因为 Scout CI 矩阵仅覆盖 gfx942/gfx950。Issue #47562

4. 性能与优化

AMD / ROCm

  • PR #47309：对 DCP indexer 进行行拆分，在 AITER asm kernel 上运行自有 sparse MLA，并对 a2a 进行流水线化（基于 #47180 / #44322 堆叠）。PR #47309
  • PR #47872：DSA decode 的单遍 Triton/Gluon top-k——在 MI355X 上 ≥72 行/rank 时为 58–82 µs 对比 113–127 µs（快 1.5–1.9×）。PR #47872
  • PR #43126：在 MI355X 上为 Kimi-K3 直接从 radix-4 router 启动发出 AITER 的 MoE sort，目标是 decode 受限的 AgentX 延迟（c16 时每次 MoE 调用约 80 tokens）。PR #43126
  • PR #49377：为 MI450（gfx1250）大张量集合通信提供 ring all-reduce 和展开的 2shot_push。PR #49377
  • PR #38806：Qwen3.5 GDN prefill——在 ROCm 上将 Q/K/V/Z/B/A 保持为 strided view，并消除额外的 QKV 拆分启动。PR #38806
  • PR #48398：GDN Triton 分块 prefill 读取 strided q/k/v 并跳过无效的输出零填充。PR #48398

正确性 / 调度

  • PR #49404：修复 EAGLE verify 将单个 repetition-penalty 行应用于所有 draft 位置的问题；现在按 draft 位置应用。PR #49404
  • PR #49386：PP 调度器在记录完成事件前等待本地 PP forward，并跳过过期的 DSpark KV 写入。PR #49386
  • PR #45180：为 MiniMax-H3 提供可选的 FP8 视频 VAE 解码器配置（逐通道 E4M3 权重、逐 token 激活缩放、融合 norm/act/quant）。PR #45180

路线图

  • PD 分离 Q4 路线图（#43699）和 Agentic Cache Scheduling Q4 路线图（#43098，超节点级 L1+L2 KV 共享，具备 router 缓存位置感知）。Issue #43699 · Issue #43098

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. SM90 decode 回归 v0.5.22 → v0.5.23 — 在 8×H20-3e 上使用 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSPARK，并发 12 时，8K–64K 上下文范围内每步 decode 时间增加 33–45%；use_deep_select_decode 在 Hopper 上也会损失接受率。尚无修复 PR。Issue #49336
  2. SM120 无法开箱即用 — CUDA 13 wheel 在 RTX 50 系列消费级 Blackwell 上安装失败；相关：#49173（现已关闭）从 DSV4.1 DeepGEMM indexer 门控中移除了 SM120/SM121，导致 GB10 上通过逐层 tolist() torch 回退出现约 8× prefill 回归。Issue #49209 · Issue #49173
  3. AMD gfx1151（Strix Halo）： MLA 形状的 Triton decode 在不规则长序列批次上返回 NaN/错误行（#48967）；--enable-deterministic-inference 在启动时失败，因为 batch-invariant matmul 需要 99 KB LDS，而可用仅 64 KB（#48968）。两者均未关闭，无关联修复。Issue #48967 · Issue #48968
  4. Breakable prefill CUDA graph 正确性 — 填充到捕获 bucket 的短 prefill 与 eager logprobs 不一致（Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4、混合 GDN、v0.5.23）。Issue #49133
  5. SM120 上的 GLM-5.3-Flash — fa4 后端在混合 extend reshape 的 CUDA-graph 捕获时崩溃；Triton 是唯一可用路径（v0.5.20 镜像）。Issue #42012
  6. Qwen-VL 解析 — 消息内容中的字面 <image> 文本会导致请求以 500 token 不匹配错误中止。Issue #43979
  7. CI/基础设施： flaky-test 跟踪器 #42752 现已有 191 条评论；Xeon SPR 任务在 sglang-spr08/18/19 上 KV 分配期间被 OOM kill（#48411）；扩散性能检查依赖主机，任务内重试无帮助（#48311）。Issue #42752 · Issue #48411 · Issue #48311

最近也因不活跃而关闭：8×H20 上 DeepSeek-V4 TP=8 245K 上下文 decode 挂起（#33549）、Kimi-K3 tool_choice=required 在 2P2D TP8/DCP8 中挂起（#37430）——如果你在旧版本上遇到其中任一问题，则相关。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 有意识地固定版本。 如果你在 Hopper 上使用推测解码服务 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash，在采用 v0.5.23 前先做基准测试——报告的 33–45% decode 减速对交互式 agent 而言影响重大。
  • SM120 消费级 Blackwell 尚不是开箱即用的目标。 RTX 50 系列和 GB10 部署应预期需要固定旧镜像、强制 Triton attention，并避免依赖 DeepGEMM indexer 路径（见 #49209、#49173、#42012）。
  • EAGLE repetition penalty 修复值得关注，如果你在使用推测解码时设置 repetition_penalty != 1——PR #49404 修正了 verify 中已知的质量偏差。
  • PD 分离和超节点 KV 缓存共享（#43699、#43098）是最影响多租户 agent 路由成本的路线图项；缓存感知多模态路由（#48937）是你服务图像聊天时的第一个实用组件。
  • 自托管扩散/视频模型的 agent 框架获得增量收益：MiniMax-H3 FP8 VAE 解码（#45180）和用于 DMD2 训练的仅轨迹 rollout 响应（#49143）。PR #49143
  • 如果你维护树外模型， 请关注 #48475——当前四个私有触点（registry、attention 查找、attention kernel、logprob sampler）在正式化之前是维护隐患。
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp

llama.cpp 摘要 — 2026-11-10

1. 今日亮点

llama.cpp 密集发布了一批版本（b12219–b12236），涵盖多模态音频重采样、外部 PLE/分片加载，以及一个长期存在的服务器 JSON-schema 修复。后端正确性获得了实质性关注：Metal flash-attention 越界写入已修补，T-TRI 获得了反向传播，ggml-backend 现在会跳过上传从未被读取的输入。模型侧，Granite NVFP4 缩放管道和 DFlash2/Kimi K3.1 视觉集成正在进行中。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

  • b12236 — mtmd_helper_resampler（详情）：为绕过 miniaudio 的原始 PCM 输入路径新增的辅助函数；修复了原始音频的重采样问题。包含文档和测试。
  • b12233 — 外部 PLE 文件加载（#31185）：--ple 现在是 --shard 的别名，并接受多个分片路径；转换器会输出独立的 PLE 导出。行为说明： 现有的单参数 --ple 脚本仍然有效，但多分片用法应予以审查。
  • b12229 — 服务器 JSON schema 修复（#28697）：OpenAI 兼容的 /v1/chat/completions 端点现在会遵循 response_format: {type: "json_schema"} 中的顶层 schema，而不再仅支持嵌套的 json_schema 包装形式。使用嵌套形式的客户端不受影响。
  • 其他版本：b12230（ggml-zdnn 张量校验）、b12228（TRI 反向传播）、b12224（后端输入上传剪枝）、b12223（Granite NVFP4）、b12221（Metal FA 越界修复）、b12220（Metal TRI 选择）、b12219（OpenCL climits 引入）。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Kimi K3.1 视觉 — PR #31980（ngxson），与 vLLM 输出对齐；修复 #31963。
  • 面向 Recursive Ripple-65B-Preview 的 DFLASH2 — PR #31904，已在 Apple M5 Max / Metal 上以 Q4_K 目标 + Q8_0 草稿模型测试。
  • 腾讯 DSpine 草稿支持 — PR #31941（Qwen3-8B-DSpine-b16、Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16），一种 DFlash 块草稿变体，每个草稿层带有一个代码桥接。
  • Gemma 4 音频流式 — PR #31965 已关闭；因果编码器在 step_ms=480 下复用 mtmd_audio_stream，最差行余弦相似度为 0.993–0.997（对比非流式）。解决 #31561。
  • Granite NVFP4 权重缩放 — PR #31449 通过 build_ffn 为所有 Granite 架构落地缩放管道（已在 b12223 中合入）。
  • OpenCL — 新增 f32 MUL_MAT_ID（#31783，已合并），对 test-llama-archs 有用。
  • OpenVINO — FILL 作为原地循环缓存清除，并修复 NaN 粘滞问题（#31977）。
  • SYCL — ROLL 算子现在能处理置换源（#31799）。
  • XDNA 后端功能请求仍然开放，社区兴趣浓厚（#21725，👍 39）。

4. 性能与优化

  • 后端上传剪枝（#31419，b12224）：ggml-backend 不再上传内容从未被读取的张量——对多后端图直接节省带宽/H2D 开销。
  • Adreno Vulkan 标量 FA 上限（#30829）：对 head size >128 且 KV ≥1024 的情况将行数上限设为 8，防止寄存器溢出（在 X1-85 上观察到每次调用 264 B）。与移动端/Qualcomm 部署相关。
  • OpenCL int8 融合 KQ（#30249）：按 head-size 切片暂存 Q，启用 head size 512，并在分解式 prefill attention 中减少随 head size 增长的本地内存。
  • ARM NEON 非 dotprod IQ4_NL_Q8 GEMM/GEMV 4×4 重打包（#30165）：将快速路径扩展到 ARMv8 < 8.2-A（无 vdotq_laneq_s32）。
  • x86 BF16 点积（#31878）：在不支持 AVX512-BF16 的 x86 上保持 F32 激活，避免重复转换和精度损失（#31842）。
  • MMVQ 截断表（#28090）：提议为 Q4_0 添加 sm_86 条目（在 A10 上约 9.1%）；仍开放。
  • Battlemage 上的 SYCL：反复出现“极其糟糕”性能的报告（#22413，现已关闭）——除非提交新 issue，否则预计不会有即时修复。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. 高 — /v1/chat/completions 上 KV 缓存被错误截断（#11970，50 条评论，仍开放）。长期存在；影响多轮对话的正确性。未引用修复 PR。
  2. 高 — 统一 KV 缓存下提示缓存恢复失败（#30961）。槽位空闲清除顺序 bug；影响服务器恢复延迟。
  3. 高 — 含 NaN 的循环状态未被清除（#29830）。NaN 传播会在循环架构上扰乱后续请求。
  4. 高 — 投机解码破坏 temp‑0 一致性（#31472）。draft-dflash / draft-dspark 即使在 100% 接受率下也偏离自回归输出——与对可复现性敏感的评估管道直接相关。与后端无关。
  5. 中 — ggml_backend_sched_alloc_splits 意外重分配崩溃（#28753），出现在 Intel Arc / IntelLLVM 构建上。
  6. 中 — SYCL+MoE 上 logprobs 非确定性（#31206）；请求 seed 无法固定分布。
  7. 中 — Metal 长上下文下 1 个 token 后解码 EOS（Qwen3.8-Flash-Next）（#28805，因过期关闭）——阈值随量化/KV 量化/n_ctx 变化。
  8. 中 — Windows AMD VRAM 误报导致共享内存溢出（#30250）。
  9. 低 — Vulkan Adreno 管道创建失败（mul_mat_vec_q4_k_f32_f32，shaderc/NDK SPIR-V 不匹配）（#28635）。
  10. 低 — ggml_gallocr 在节点身份变化时复用过期计划（#28448，因过期关闭）——存在静默稀疏 MoE 损坏风险。

今日/本周期已修复： Metal FA 越界写入（#31662，b12221）；Metal TRI ±inf→NaN（#30711，b12220）；Qwen4exp 合并张量断言（#31189，已关闭）；json_schema response_format（#10732，已关闭）。

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • OpenAI 兼容性正在收紧。 response_format 中的顶层 json_schema 现在可用（b12229）——你可以去掉包装 hack。但 KV 缓存截断（#11970）和提示缓存恢复失败（#30961）仍然开放，因此对长多轮会话要保守，并考虑在服务器端使用固定/扩展上下文。
  • 投机解码的可复现性注意事项。 如果你在 --temp 0 下运行评估或确定性 agent，在 #31472 解决之前，避免在 qwen35moe 目标上使用 draft-dflash/draft-dspark——输出与 AR 解码并非 token 级一致。
  • SYCL+MoE 上的非确定性 logprobs（#31206）意味着在 Intel iGPU + MoE 配置上，不要依赖 /v1/completions 的 logprobs 进行评分/重排序。
  • 多模态音频正在获得一等公民地位。 mtmd_helper_resampler（b12236）+ Gemma 4 流式（余弦 ≥0.993 对比非流式）使 /v1/audio/* 和实时端点对生产语音 agent 变得可行——预计 #31763 会带来更多 /v1/audio/speech 工作。
  • token 感知的聊天解析即将到来（#29307、#31978）。如果你从原始输出中自行解析 <think>/工具调用 token，请计划在它落地后迁移到服务器发出的结构化字段——这将比字符串匹配更健壮。
  • 新的草稿模型架构（DSpine、DFLASH2、Kimi K3.1 视觉）持续扩展投机解码和多模态面；请针对你的目标量化和后端进行验证——目前有几个仅在 Metal/CUDA 上测试过。
  • Windows AMD 用户：VRAM 误报（#30250）可能悄悄推入共享内存并拖垮吞吐量；请监控你实际的 VRAM 余量，而不是信任运行时报告的内存预算。

Ollama 摘要 — 2026-11-10

4. 性能与优化

  • VRAM 核算与 GPU 拆分（进行中）：PR #19632（issue #19631）修复错误的 VRAM 预测、GPU 开销预留以及不必要的模型拆分，后者导致了错误的驱逐和加载拒绝—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19632
  • Vulkan 提示缓存回归：Issue #19201（已关闭）记录了在启用捆绑的 llama.cpp 主机内存提示缓存时，第二次相同请求出现可复现的约 29.7 倍生成吞吐量崩塌，AMD RX 6600 XT / Mesa RADV，Ollama 0.40.8—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19201
  • num_predict == -2 动态 token 限制（填充上下文缓冲区）PR #9547 已关闭—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/9547
  • Qwen3.5 4B 提示处理指导 在 16GB M4（100% GPU）上被请求；未确认缺陷—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19282

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  1. CUDA 预热失败 + 静默 CPU 回退 — Issue #17380（开放）：Windows/RTX 5070 Ti 上使用 gpt-oss:20b 时间歇性出现 CUDA error: shared object initialization failed，与静默的 CUDA_Host → CPU 固定缓冲区回退相关；未引用修复 PR—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17380
  2. Windows 更新器崩溃 — Issue #19621（开放）：IsProcRunning 将 EnumProcesses 的字节计数当作 PID 计数，当运行超过 512 个进程时 panic；同日打开修复 PR #19625—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19621 · https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19625
  3. Qwen3.5 4B 仅思考响应 — Issue #18916（开放）：使用 num_ctx:65536 的长对话返回 done:true 但只有 message.thinking，无内容/工具调用—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/18916
  4. 工具调用压缩不匹配 — Issue #19623（开放）：在 Codex Desktop + DeepSeek 中重复压缩保留了函数输出但没有匹配的调用—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19623
  5. VRAM 报告差异 — Issue #17251（开放）：使用 MTP 加速器模型时，ollama ps 相对于 rocm-smi 低报了 VRAM—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/17251
  6. 企业代理拉取 403 — Issue #19604（已关闭）：在 Blue Coat 代理后 ollama pull 返回 403，尽管 curl 正常工作—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/19604
  7. Olmo3 工具参数中的 Unicode 损坏 — PR #18906（开放）修复 splitArguments 中的 UTF-8 截断—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/18906
  8. Modelfile glob 路径解析 — PR #19628（开放）：当路径包含 glob 元字符时，相对通配符针对字面目录解析—— https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/19628

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • OpenAI 兼容客户端：/v1/models 空数组变更是在客户端代码中需要测试的一项行为——将零安装模型视为有效状态，而非错误。/v1/responses 中的截断转发提升了与 OpenAI 语义的对等性。
  • 结构化工具调用：如果你使用 Codex/DeepSeek 风格的压缩循环，请固定版本并关注 #19623——孤立的函数输出可能破坏代理状态机。使用非 ASCII 参数的 Olmo3 用户应跟踪 #18906。
  • VRAM 敏感部署： #19632 调度器修复直接解决了错误的驱逐和不必要的多 GPU 拆分——这是采用此 RC 之后下一个稳定版的强有力理由。目前，在确定容量之前，请对照 rocm-smi/nvidia-smi 验证 ollama ps 数字。
  • Qwen3.5 并行性：一旦 #17144 落地，MoE 服务吞吐量增益将可用；在此之前，这些架构预期 numParallel=1。
  • Windows 集群运维：超过 512 个进程的更新器崩溃（#19621/#19625）意味着繁忙主机上的自动部署工具应分阶段进行，而非完全无人值守，直到修复发布。

由 github.com/ollama/ollama 2026-11-10 数据快照生成。

LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM 摘要 — 2026-11-10

1. 今日要点

v1.108.4 发布，附带 cosign 签名的 Docker 镜像（验证密钥在 commit e82a3c6 中引入）。Issue 队列被成本/预算正确性问题占据：一个按团队按模型限流器以配置值的一半执行限制（已关闭），以及围绕 DB 存储部署、过期重置行和缓存驱逐缺口的多起预算核算 bug。PR 方面，工作正收敛于原生（Rust 后端）/v1/messages 代理路径——一个由七个 PR 组成的栈，修复日志、缓存、流式中断和失败行计费——外加向 1.108.x 和 1.109.0 发布分支的回移。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

  • v1.108.4 — 通过 cosign 对 Docker 镜像签名；验证密钥见发布说明。Release
  • 即将到来的 2.0.0 行为变更（已预告）： 密钥或团队上空的 models 列表表示“所有模型”的遗留规则将被移除。PR #50720 增加了启动时警告，统计依赖此默认值的密钥/团队，并记录了迁移路径。PR #50720
  • litellm.turn_on_message_logging 文档 bug 已关闭 — 实际 API 是 turn_off_message_logging。Issue #37143

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Claude “fable-5-2”（Fable 5.2） 的能力标志和提示缓存定价正从 Anthropic API 扩展到 Vertex AI 和 Bedrock Converse，并添加了线格式和成本测试。PR #50742
  • Z.AI glm-5.2[1m]（1M 上下文变体）已有文档，但通过代理返回 Unknown Model — 仍处于打开状态。Issue #32218
  • 自定义命名部署（例如 Azure AI Foundry 上服务 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 的 my-flash）的 tokenizer 解析现在使用配置的 base_model tokenizer，而不是回退到 OpenAI 的。PR #50734
  • Rust 后端 pip 二进制工作继续作为安装问题的跟踪 issue。Issue #31261

4. 性能与优化

  • 浪费的 Redis 写入： 限流器无条件写入调用后计数器，即使对于未配置任何限制的密钥/用户/团队也是如此。已提议修复以在高吞吐量下跳过这些写入；PR 已陈旧，但 issue 仍处于打开状态。Issue #31880
  • 基于成本路由下的提示/压缩节省： 当同一模型名有多个部署时，compression_savings_spend 和 prompt_caching_savings_spend 始终为 $0 — 已关闭。Issue #37117
  • 缓存读取计费： azure/us/gpt-4o-2024-11-20 和 azure/eu/... 缺少 cache_read_input_token_cost，导致缓存读取按零计费 — 已关闭。Issue #37823
  • 原生 /v1/messages 路径： 缓存条目现在在路由器标记响应之后写入（与 Python 行为一致），流中途客户端断开连接也能正确计费 — 这是七个 PR 栈的一部分。PR #50426, PR #50425

5. 稳定性与回归（按严重程度排序）

高

  • 限流器将按团队按模型限制减半： model_per_team 的 RPM/TPM 为 N 时在约 N/2 处返回 429。已提交精确复现；已关闭。Issue #34140
  • 预算重置任务静默地将支出永久清零： 一行 budget_duration=null 但 budget_reset_at 为过期过去时间的记录每个 tick 都被拾取，无限期清除支出。已关闭。Issue #39370
  • 项目预算绕过原子预留： 项目最大预算仅在读取时生效，从未参与调用前预留路径，因此并发请求可能超支。已关闭。Issue #34101
  • 通过过期的单 pod 支出绕过最终用户预算： 在 Redis 计数器干净未命中（60s TTL）时，过期的 pod 本地回退值可能放行请求。已关闭。Issue #34238
  • 已删除的团队密钥仍具认证有效性： /team/delete 从 DB 中移除密钥，但从未将其从认证缓存中驱逐。已关闭。Issue #34217

中

  • 流式用量在链式代理设置（Front → Upstream → Bedrock）中严重少计，而非流式用量正确；根因追溯到流聚合，而非提供商转换。打开。Issue #36114
  • JSON-RPC id 被剥离，由 pass_through_endpoints 因与内部参数名冲突导致 — 破坏 JSON-RPC 2.0 载荷。打开。Issue #49479
  • 价格重载清除 DB 部署成本映射： 在空 model_list + STORE_MODEL_IN_DB 下，定期成本映射重载丢弃运行时成本注册（路由器不在 _live_routers 中）。已关闭。Issue #43444
  • Presidio PII 去掩码缺口： 工具调用参数从未去掩码（#31950，打开），且占位符按消息编号导致跨消息损坏（#31959，打开）。
  • reasoning_effort=xhigh 在模型映射缺少能力时被静默降级，而非被拒绝。已关闭。Issue #40471
  • general_settings 中的 completion_model 覆盖客户端模型，而非作为回退。打开，陈旧。Issue #21554
  • VSCode 原生模型提供商与 LiteLLM 不兼容。打开。Issue #35775

低

  • /v1/messages 流式在 Bedrock 推理模型的内容块转换处丢弃第一个 chunk。已关闭。Issue #25214
  • Ollama 流式为所有工具调用发出 index=0，将并行调用合并为畸形 JSON。已关闭。Issue #33678
  • token_counter 在数组工具参数缺少 items 时抛出 KeyError: 'items' → /v1/messages/count_tokens 上 500。已关闭。Issue #46052
  • Azure 请求泄漏内部 model_alias_map 字段，被上游拒绝。已关闭。Issue #42409
  • Bedrock count_tokens 在畸形请求体上返回 500 而非 400；已在 PR #50708 中修复。
  • 不稳定的 MCP 测试 test_cold_concurrent_schema_validation_accepts_valid_arguments。已关闭。Issue #46212

进行中的修复 PR

  • Bedrock 直通拒绝原始 AWS 模型 ID（POST /bedrock/model/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5/converse → 400）— PR #50737
  • /v1/messages 在不受支持参数检查之前忽略 additional_drop_params（回移 + 主分支）— PR #50755, #50753
  • 故障关闭预算执行对缺少成员行的团队用户返回 503 — PR #50603
  • Bedrock Converse/Responses 上空的最终用户消息被丢弃，导致 Claude 5.x 预填充 400 — PR #50701
  • 路由器默认元数据替换而非合并调用方元数据 — PR #50700
  • Responses WebSocket：仅第一个被拒绝的轮次获得失败行 — PR #50731
  • Claude Code 子代理流量在复杂度路由器中覆盖主代理层级固定 — PR #50741

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 如果你使用按团队按模型上限，请审计你的限流。 减半 bug（#34140）意味着有效吞吐量可能只有配置的一半；升级后重新检查，并在依赖 model_per_team 实现 SLA 式隔离前进行负载测试。
  • 预算执行在历史上多条路径上存在漏洞（项目预算、过期重置行、缓存未命中回退）。如果你依赖硬性支出上限实现租户隔离，请通过并发负载验证而非信任仪表盘，并保留外部支出告警作为兜底。
  • 删除团队不会立即撤销密钥（在受影响版本上）— 对已停用团队的密钥进行轮换或显式 /key/delete。
  • 链式代理部署会少计流式用量。 如果你在多跳设置中基于 LiteLLM 的用量数字向下游计费，请与提供商侧账单对账（#36114）。
  • PII 护栏用户： Presidio 掩码对工具调用参数和多消息请求不完整 — 不要将其作为带工具的代理工作负载的唯一 DLP 层。
  • 现在为 2.0.0 空 models 语义变更做规划： 在密钥和团队上显式枚举允许的模型，并关注新的启动警告（#50720）以发现遗留配置。
  • 原生 /v1/messages 路径正在成熟（被放弃流的计费、缓存写入顺序、每 WebSocket 轮次的失败行）。如果你大规模使用 Claude Code 或 Anthropic 协议客户端，预计在 1.108.x/1.109 系列中计量准确性会有所改善。
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth 摘要 — 2026-11-10

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时没有新版本发布，但 main 分支上堆叠了大量推理引擎相关的工作：Daniel Han 提交了一系列 decode CUDA graph PR（#16587 为基础，外加针对 Gemma 4 和 Qwen3.5/3.6 的模型专属扩展），声称在 T4 上实现 2–8 倍 decode 加速，且输出 token 完全一致。与此同时，Studio 的模型服务层（面向前端本地模型的 HTTP 网关）积累了几个与 OpenAI 兼容端点相关的 issue——尤其是自定义/vLLM/Ollama 连接下视频被静默拒绝的问题，但修复 PR 已开放（#17322）。

2. 版本发布与破坏性变更

无新版本发布。有一个依赖锁定隐患值得注意：typer 0.29.0（发布于 2026-11-09 18:48 UTC）会导致 Windows 上的 Studio 安装失败，原因是它持有 pydantic_core 不放。将 typer 限制在 <0.29 的修复已合并（#17319）。如果你基于 Studio 安装器构建，在 Windows 上请避免使用未锁定版本的 typer。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Gemma 4、Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6（qwen3_5、qwen3_5_moe） — CUDA graph 下的 flex-attention decode 步骤（#17329）。
  • Qwen3.5/3.6 混合线性注意力（Gated DeltaNet） — 为 LinearAttentionLayer 静态缓存提供 decode graph 支持，此前该场景被直接拒绝（#17324）。
  • 基础 decode-graph PR 中的文本模型广泛覆盖：Gemma 3/4、Muse-Glimmer、Qwen3 / Qwen3-VL text、Llama、Mistral 3、Granite、Phi-4、OLMo 2、Cohere 2、GLM-4（#16587）。
  • Linux GPU 检测回归 — issue 报告支持 CUDA 的 Linux 主机被强制使用 CPU（#17235，已关闭）。另有报告称 Windows 图像生成在 RTX 3060 上回退到内存（#16803，已关闭）。

4. 性能与优化

  • 所有 FastModel model.generate() 默认启用 decode CUDA graph — 重放捕获的单 token 步骤，而非承担内核启动开销；在 T4 上实测2–8 倍提升，输出 token 完全一致（#16587）。
  • 可选启用的可增长 KV 缓存（UNSLOTH_GROWABLE_KV=1）— 避免 StaticCache 为每个全注意力层预分配 prompt + max_new_tokens。默认关闭；未设置时行为零变化（#17296）。
  • Studio / WebKit 长对话性能系列 — 多个 PR 针对菜单/对话框/浏览器面板打开成本随对话长度增长的问题：通过消除每帧线程工作和重新布局，150 轮基准从约 460–560 ms 降至短对话水平（#17282、#17284、#17323）。
  • MCP 工具循环低效 — 启用大量 MCP 工具时，GGUF 对话几乎每条消息都重新处理整个 prompt；开放中的 PR 保留延迟工具定义（#17326，追踪自 #17015）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按服务型工作负载的严重程度排序：

  1. 自定义 OpenAI 兼容连接（vLLM/OMLX/llama.cpp/Ollama）下视频上传被拒绝，即使后端支持视频（#17295）。修复 PR 已开放：#17322。
  2. Linux 被强制从 GPU 降级到 CPU — 已关闭，但对受影响者而言是硬性降级（#17235）。
  3. Studio 网页抓取的 HTML→Markdown 转换器 bug — 裸 & 后残留 ;、代码围栏内逃逸内容泄漏、畸形实体导致后续页面内容按原始 HTML 渲染（#17199）。如果你依赖抓取工具的输出质量或将其送入下游解析，此问题值得关注。
  4. 托管账户文件夹浏览 403 — 安装为符号链接时 /api/models/browse-folders 返回 403；影响多租户 Studio 部署（#17292，修复 PR #17321）。
  5. typer 0.29 导致 Windows 安装失败 — 修复已合并（#17319）。
  6. 附件注释解析器误报 — 文件内容形似沙箱附件注释时被解析为第二个附件（#16913，已关闭）。
  7. TRL 1.15 下 CPU SFTTrainer 评估损失错误 — 除以未移位的标签数量，导致首个 token 未被掩码时 eval_loss 被低估（#17291）。修复了纯 CPU 微调流程的损失曲线失真问题。
  8. ROCM TunableOp 测试回归 — 自 #17299 起 main 上出现回归，修复 PR 已开放（#17325）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • Decode 吞吐量即将免费获得实质性提升。 如果你通过 FastModel.generate() 服务 Qwen3.x/Llama/Gemma 级模型，默认启用的 decode graph 应在较旧 GPU（T4 级）上带来多倍 token 速率提升，且输出不变。下个版本发布后值得基准测试你的 p50/p99 延迟；同时，请验证对确定性敏感的评估仍然一致。
  • 可增长 KV 缓存的可选启用值得长上下文服务关注。 固定 StaticCache 的过度分配一直是并发长 prompt 工作负载的真实瓶颈；如果你运行高 max_new_tokens 但实际生成量不大，发布后可试用 UNSLOTH_GROWABLE_KV=1。
  • 目前还不要信任"自定义 OpenAI 兼容"的多模态能力 — 视频在客户端就被拒绝，根本到不了 vLLM/Ollama。在修复落地前，请锁定到修复 PR 或在本地模型加载上验证。
  • Studio 正在积累一个真正的 OpenAI 兼容网关表面（自定义端点、MCP 工具、网页抓取、托管账户）。该层的 bug 密度——权限模式仅限会话（#17297）、偏好同步缺口（#16912）、MCP prompt 重复处理——表明它目前仍在成熟过程中，尚未达到可用于生产级 agent 路由的加固程度。
  • 如果你在桌面上做图像 LoRA 或大规模语料索引，资源管理仍需手动：项目索引没有暂停/限流机制，可能饿死推理（#16992，已关闭），图像 LoRA 训练也缺少可复用的设置配置（#16979，已关闭）。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-10

Generated: 2026-11-09 23:19 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Ecosystem

Digest Date: 2026-11-10

1. Ecosystem Overview

Today's activity confirms a two-tier infrastructure landscape: serving engines (vLLM, SGLang) are in a hardware-enablement trench war — SM120/GB10 consumer Blackwell and MI355X/MI450 now consume the majority of issue and PR bandwidth, with correctness regressions (silent empty completions, silent kernel output corruption) outnumbering feature work. The local/edge tier (llama.cpp, Ollama, Unsloth) is shipping at high velocity but is fragmenting along backends (Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, ROCm, OpenCL, XDNA), with reproducibility and KV-cache correctness as the recurring weak point. Gateways (LiteLLM) are consolidating on metering correctness — a stack of closed budget/rate-limit bypass bugs and a native Rust-backed /v1/messages path signal that billing accuracy is now the primary competitive axis. Across all layers, speculative decoding is maturing into the default throughput lever while simultaneously generating the largest cluster of correctness regressions (EAGLE/MTP/DFlash/DFlash2/DSpine divergence, acceptance collapse at TP>1). Notably absent: no releases from vLLM, SGLang, or Unsloth in the last 24h — the day's work is integration and bug-fixing, not shipping.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Layer Issues Referenced PRs Referenced Release Status (24h) Dominant Theme

Concentration read: Three distinct battles are visible. (a) AMD is a first-class performance target — SGLang has the deepest MI355X/MI450 kernel pipeline (DSA top-k, ring all-reduce, AITER asm MLA); vLLM is chasing with ROCm AITER MLA (but hit a closed critical silent-corruption bug, #66141). (b) KV-cache capacity is the universal bottleneck — vLLM recovers it via workspace tuning, Unsloth via growable allocation, SGLang via supernode sharing; the Vulkan prompt-cache 30× regression in Ollama is the cautionary counterexample. (c) Decode-graph adoption is spreading outward from training frameworks — Unsloth's default-on CUDA graphs delivering 2–8× on T4 is the single largest headline throughput claim in the digest set, and it directly competes with serving engines for the "small-model, high-throughput" use case.

Gateway / control plane LiteLLM Routing, rate limiting, budgets, cost accounting, provider normalization, PII guardrails The gateway is becoming a metering and policy enforcement point — this week's issue cluster (5 High-severity budget/rate-limit bypasses, all closed) proves the layer is still hardening. Native Rust /v1/messages (7-PR stack) is an infrastructure-language migration for the hot path.

It is now a credible single-machine alternative to a serving engine for Qwen/Llama/Gemma-class workloads. Training-side correctness (CPU eval loss #17291) is the current gap.

Buyer's framing: vLLM/SGLang = scale-out multi-tenant serving; llama.cpp = maximum hardware portability and model breadth; Ollama = developer-experience and distribution; LiteLLM = multi-provider governance and cost control; Unsloth = fine-tune-then-serve in one stack. These are complementary, not substitutable — the interesting overlap is Unsloth vs local serving engines, and LiteLLM vs native provider SDKs.

6. Trend Signals

1. Silent correctness failures are the new availability risk. Two CRITICAL-grade issues this week return HTTP 200 with wrong content: vLLM's NVFP4 MoE empty completions on SM120 (#51525, content: null + finish_reason: length) and the closed-but-verify ROCm AITER MLA uncorrelated output (#66141). Combined with llama.cpp's spec-decode temp-0 divergence (#31472) and SGLang's breakable prefill CUDA-graph divergence (#49133), the message is clear: output validation must be part of the serving stack, not the application's assumption.

2. Speculative decoding is the throughput default and the correctness frontier. Every project touched it today — vLLM (EAGLE/MTP prefix-cache block-drop, 30–40% batch loss; DFlash TP>1 collapse), SGLang (EAGLE repetition-penalty skew fix), llama.cpp (DFLASH2/DSpine, temp-0 divergence), Unsloth (decode graphs). Developers running reproducibility-sensitive evals or deterministic agents should disable spec decode or pin versions until per-project fix matrix lands.

3. AMD is no longer a secondary target — it's a co-primary. SGLang has a dense MI355X/MI450 PR stream; vLLM has MI355X performance trackers and a "MonoKernel" proposal (#60904); llama.cpp and Ollama carry ongoing ROCm/Vulkan issues (RDNA AWQ 2.5× slower, gfx1151 NaN, VRAM misreporting). Fleet standardization should treat ROCm as a distinct, pinning-heavy environment — not a drop-in for CUDA paths.

4. Consumer Blackwell (SM120/GB10) is a broken tier out-of-the-box across both serving engines. vLLM (CUDA-graph failures, silent empty completions) and SGLang (CUDA 13 wheel install fails; ~8× prefill regression from DSV4.1 DeepGEMM gate removal, #49173) independently confirm SM120 is not production-ready for quantized MoE or long-context today. Blackwell datacenter (SM100/SM90) is fine; consumer SKUs are the gap.

5. Gateways are becoming the audited control plane. LiteLLM's five closed High-severity budget/rate-limit bypasses (project budgets outside reservation path, stale-reset zeroing spend, deleted-team key auth-cache retention, per-team-model limit halving) plus the pre-announced 2.0.0 empty-models semantics change mean agent/application developers should: audit limits post-upgrade, reconcile streaming usage against provider bills in chained-proxy topologies (#36114), and enumerate allowed models explicitly before the deprecation window closes.

6. OpenAI compatibility is tablestakes, structure emission is the innovation. llama.cpp's top-level json_schema fix (b12229), Ollama's /v1/models empty-array change and truncation forwarding, and Unsloth Studio's custom-endpoint gateway all converge on OpenAI wire-compat. The next step is schema-enforced structured generation — llama.cpp's token-aware chat parsing (#29307/#31978) is migrating <think>/tool-call parsing from client-side string matching to server-emitted fields. Plan that migration for agent frameworks.

7. What to watch next week:

  • vLLM: whether Marlin→Humming migration lands with parity; SM120 CUDA-graph fix for DeepSeek-V4.1.
  • SGLang: v0.5.22→v0.5.23 decode regression resolution (material for DeepSeek-V4.1 interactive agents); MI450 all-reduce landing.
  • llama.cpp: KV-cache truncation (#11970) and prompt-cache restore (#30961) — both are long-standing HIGH and affect multi-turn correctness.
  • Ollama: stable after v0.40.16-rc0 and the #19632 VRAM accounting fix — the strongest reason to upgrade this cycle.
  • LiteLLM: 2.0.0 migration tooling; native /v1/messages stack completion for Anthropic-protocol clients.
  • Unsloth: decode-graph GA with determinism verification; growable KV release; whether Studio matures into a credible agent-routing gateway or remains a dev tool.
